# Principles

32 principles in eight stages (P15 merged into P05 in v1.1). Each line of support is computed from the research claim database; `confidence` is about the evidence, not about the principle's fit to your case.

- Stage II — Conceive

## Stage I — Frame

*Why must this exist, for whom, against what?*

### P01 Start from the reason the work must exist

Name the purpose before ideation — why this project must exist and what gap it fills — and use it as the test for every later choice; when execution drifts from it, correct toward it rather than accept the drift.

- Limits: Purpose is the user's; the lens can sharpen it, never invent it. 'Go back to the start' is one 2015 remark, not a documented routine.
- Guards against: Ideation from an aimless reference pile; drift during production.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-34 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 10 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-002, MHJ-CL-003, MHJ-CL-137

### P02 Treat the brief's category words as questions

Interrogate stock words in the brief ("trendy", "Gen Z", "premium", "girl group", "worldview") until each carries a specific idea; industry vocabulary can hide what people actually experience.

- Limits: Do not rename things for novelty; legal, administrative or regulated terms keep their official wording.
- Guards against: Executing a cliché literally.
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 13 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-005, MHJ-CL-139, MHJ-CL-140, MHJ-CL-073

### P03 Find the meaning the project already owns

Look first for meaning in what the project already has — its name, its core activity, its people's real but under-shown traits, the archetype of its main object — before importing an outside theme.

- Limits: A tendency, not a law: she has also chosen a name for how the letters look and attached meanings afterwards (ooak, 2026). Archetype is a starting point, not a period costume (P11).
- Guards against: Decorative themes with no root in the subject.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-32 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 12 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-006, MHJ-CL-007, MHJ-CL-046

### P04 Size the audience by who does not yet care

Aim growth at people outside the category, not only at existing fans; design for a specific, true emotion that can travel across age, gender and genre rather than for a demographic, and treat 'what the public wants' as an assumption to test.

- Limits: Her premise that fans would 'come anyway' rested on attention her name already had (MHJ-CL-083); without that, plan how the first audience is reached.
- Guards against: Persona-and-demographic targeting; preaching to the converted.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-35, MHJ-CX-37, MHJ-CX-34 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 14 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-092, MHJ-CL-093, MHJ-CL-098, MHJ-CL-099

### P05 Position against the context; test newness for a reason

Identify the surrounding house style or environment and the felt-but-unnamed gap in it, then stand out by contrast rather than by escalating polish. Test every 'new' move for a reason: a surface swap is not change, and when an audience is bored the frame must change, not the decoration.

- Limits: Contrast must have a reason; contrarianism for its own sake is another formula.
- Guards against: Me-too work; louder versions of what is already there; cosmetic refreshes sold as reinvention.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-34 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 18 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-137, MHJ-CL-027, MHJ-CL-089, MHJ-CL-026, MHJ-CL-028, MHJ-CL-068

## Stage II — Conceive

*What is the idea, and where does it come from?*

### P06 The concept is the whole experience

Treat the concept as the felt whole across material, image, styling, product, release sequence and behaviour — not the visual layer — and design how it will be met at the same time as the thing itself.

- Limits: In a small task (a single headline, one screen) apply only the relevant part.
- Guards against: Concept = moodboard; marketing bolted on afterwards.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-25, MHJ-CX-30 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 11 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-011, MHJ-CL-069, MHJ-CL-074

### P07 Derive the idea from the material's first impression

Begin from the first image or scene the core material itself evokes (for her, usually the music) and only then reach for outside references; keep a bank of stored ideas and pick the one most interesting to tell with this material.

- Limits: Outside music, 'material' is the product, service, data or place. Her own framing moved from 'visualising music' (SM) to 'music first' (ADOR); no fixed hierarchy between media is implied.
- Guards against: Reference-board-first concepts that could fit any client.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-31 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 15 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-001, MHJ-CL-039, MHJ-CL-004

### P08 Translate the impression; never copy the surface

Take a reference's impression, energy or structure, not its surface; carrying it into a different medium (sound into image, image into an action) is the most reliable way to avoid copying. Choose references for one consistent sensibility, often from outside the category, and raise the overlooked to a major standard of finish.

- Limits: Same-medium borrowing also appears in her work (a cover inspired by a film image, a stage cover of a song); what is avoided is reproducing the surface. Her 'whole-combination' originality threshold was stated in a 2024 copying dispute and her own catalogue faces open allegations (CX-41, CX-46; no merits judged).
- Guards against: Pastiche; reference-matching; 'make it look like X'.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-41, MHJ-CX-46 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 18 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-030, MHJ-CL-031, MHJ-CL-032, MHJ-CL-033, MHJ-CL-035

### P09 Build from a deliberate mismatch; set the emotional target precisely

Pair unlike things on purpose (mainstream subject with an outside maker; fantasy inside an ordinary setting). Define the emotional target precisely — often as a tension between two feelings — rather than one generic mood.

- Limits: Her own recurring emotional palette (bright melancholy, 'dry' beauty) is her taste, not the method; derive the user's emotional target from their material.
- Guards against: Single-note mood; predictable matching.
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 10 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-014, MHJ-CL-015, MHJ-CL-050

### P10 Coherence from a consistent reason, not lore

Hold a stable core reason and let each release or application vary its surface; treat releases as chapters that answer earlier ones; avoid constructed 'worldview' systems and fixed forms that close off later developments.

- Limits: Open premises still need a reason; tension with fictional launch devices is noted (contradiction index).
- Guards against: Lore that becomes homework; identical repetition.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-32 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 14 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-012, MHJ-CL-013, MHJ-CL-029, MHJ-CL-067

### P11 Aim at the durable feeling; period looks are means, not briefs

Aim at what people are drawn to across eras; treat trends as what the public copies after a convincing move, so chasing them makes you second. Period material may enter only as an ingredient that expresses something about the present work, never as the brief.

- Limits: 'Retro was never the target' is her stated intent, given in reply to readings of her work; it does not settle how audiences read the output (CX-21, CX-24). She chose a nostalgic direction for at least one record.
- Guards against: Y2K / retro / film-grain defaults; trend-chasing.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-21, MHJ-CX-24 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 14 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-022, MHJ-CL-023, MHJ-CL-024, MHJ-CL-141, MHJ-CL-143

## Stage III — Edit

*What stays, what goes, and is the newness real?*

### P12 Subtract toward the essential; quality lives in execution

Edit by removal toward the essential element and cut decoration that serves no use; locate quality in how well a form is executed, not in the form chosen or the money spent.

- Limits: She values both density of finish and some looseness and has criticised work that is 'too dense from the start'; she does not reconcile them (contradiction noted). 'Leave gaps' is recorded as her taste, not a rule.
- Guards against: Over-decoration; over-polish that reads as sameness.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-30 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 9 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-016, MHJ-CL-020

### P13 Intuitive is encoded, not literal

Literal work delivers a childish thing childishly; intuitive work is encoded with thought yet decodes instantly. Calibrate friction: neither so easy it tires nor so hard it shuts people out, and leave meanings open enough to set imagination working.

- Limits: Her emphasis shifted from 'slightly unfriendly' (SM) to 'decoded effortlessly' (ADOR) (MHJ-CL-061); public-service work sits at the effortless end.
- Guards against: Obviousness mistaken for clarity; obscurity mistaken for depth.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-33 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 13 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-008, MHJ-CL-009, MHJ-CL-010, MHJ-CL-061

### P14 Every visible element carries meaning

Hold small details to the standard of the whole — objects in frame, one signature per person, light, sound and material checked physically — and treat a brand as continuous curation that is maintained after launch.

- Limits: HYBE HQ was a group design; the architects claim the grid and racks (CX-43). Proportion: detail serves the purpose.
- Guards against: Defaults left in by neglect.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-43, MHJ-CX-30 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 9 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-019, MHJ-CL-021, MHJ-CL-066

### P16 List the category's reflexes, then decide each one

List the moves a category performs by reflex (its default release ritual, default structure, default visual shorthand, default incentive mechanics) and decide each on its merits: keep with a reason, drop with a reason, or change.

- Limits: Her own list (obligatory high notes, inserted raps, knife-sync dance, ritual teasers) reflects her dislikes, not universal defects; she also used random version packing she says she dislikes (CX-27). Keep conventions that serve accessibility, safety, law or trust.
- Guards against: Formula production; also contrarian removal of useful conventions.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-27, MHJ-CX-36 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 10 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-041, MHJ-CL-138

## Stage IV — Identity & language

*How is it named, marked and spoken about?*

### P17 Identity rigidity matches the brand's rate of change

Use a fixed mark only where it does structural work; otherwise build flexible marks that transform and extend; design single forms that hold several readings and leave viewers room to find them.

- Limits: Institutions that need recognisability and trust (public services, finance) may need more fixity. Institutions that need recognisability and trust (public services, finance) usually need more fixity.
- Guards against: Rigid guidelines for a brand that must keep changing register, and the reverse.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-14, MHJ-CX-15 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 13 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-053, MHJ-CL-063, MHJ-CL-064, MHJ-CL-010

### P18 Never declare quality or benefit; name intuitively

Do not announce that the work is premium, healing or special — work loses value the moment it proclaims itself and benefits imposed from above feel condescending; make the experience good and let it be noticed. Names should land at once, need no explanation, and may carry a light double reading.

- Limits: Functional, legal, price and safety information must be stated plainly; this concerns value claims, not facts. In public services, finance, health, law or safety contexts, accuracy, accessibility and official wording come first; apply only where it cannot mislead or exclude anyone (our application).
- Guards against: Copy that tells instead of shows; cringe benefit words.
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 11 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-060, MHJ-CL-096, MHJ-CL-102, MHJ-CL-144, MHJ-CL-071, MHJ-CL-072, MHJ-CL-073

## Stage V — Product

*What does the object or service do in someone's hands?*

### P19 The object performs the idea

Make the product's real-world use carry the meaning (a gift that is given, a phone-shot film about phones); let form follow the material instead of a platform rule; give each asset its own job instead of making every asset chase one metric.

- Limits: Usability comes first where the object is a tool.
- Guards against: Packaging as decoration; one-size assets.
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 13 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-055, MHJ-CL-056, MHJ-CL-111, MHJ-CL-042, MHJ-CL-088

### P20 Stated stance: earn through quality and keepsakes, not inflation tactics *(supporting — stated stance, weaker evidence)*

Her stated stance: answer the discomfort of earning from people who like the work with quality rather than extraction, make goods as keepsakes tied to a moment, and avoid tactics that inflate metrics so demand shows what is real.

- Limits: Self-account with no outcome data; much of it voiced in the dispute window. Counter-cases on record: ten-package releases at SM (2013), random version packing (2024), revenue-aimed collaboration shops (CX-26, CX-27).
- Guards against: Gacha mechanics, push-out sales, vanity numbers.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-26, MHJ-CX-27 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, medium confidence, 10 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-095, MHJ-CL-107, MHJ-CL-135, MHJ-CL-084, MHJ-CL-136

## Stage VI — Launch

*In what order, at what moment, through which sense is it met?*

### P21 Every reveal has a reason for its moment, order and medium

Design the launch with the work: decide what is seen first, in which sense (moving image over stills when the feeling needs sound), in what order and at what moment, and give each reveal a reason for its position.

- Limits: Public-service or safety launches cannot withhold information people need. 'Plan peaks backwards from the culminating event' rests on dispute-era remarks only and is not part of the rule.
- Guards against: Launch-by-calendar; ritual rollouts.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-36 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 10 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-074, MHJ-CL-075, MHJ-CL-079, MHJ-CL-080, MHJ-CL-151

### P22 Curiosity over pitch; the teaser is a tool, not a ritual

Turn what cannot yet be shown into something worth discovering, and choose teasers or no teasers by the situation; market by provoking curiosity rather than by pitching.

- Limits: Curiosity works when attention or trust already exists (MHJ-CL-083). Withholding must reward, never tease (she dislikes push-and-pull; CX-29); never withhold price, terms, safety or access information. In public services, finance, health, law or safety contexts, accuracy, accessibility and official wording come first; apply only where it cannot mislead or exclude anyone (our application).
- Guards against: Over-explaining; hype that the work cannot meet.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-29, MHJ-CX-35, MHJ-CX-36 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 10 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-076, MHJ-CL-078, MHJ-CL-082

### P23 Give the audience something to do

Offer participation rather than only viewing — decoding, customising, copying, varying — and treat a pleasurable surprise as a deliverable even in obligatory formats.

- Limits: Participation must be optional and low-friction for people who just want the thing.
- Guards against: Passive broadcast; joyless obligatory formats.
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 13 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-101, MHJ-CL-090, MHJ-CL-097

## Stage VII — Direct people

*How do specialists and performers get the idea without losing their own?*

### P24 Brief the reason behind the impression, not the look

Give specialists the purpose, context and the reason behind the feeling — at most one optional image and a few anchor items — then hand over method; withhold reference images where copying is the risk.

- Limits: Inexperienced teams may need more scaffolding; adjust (P25).
- Guards against: Moodboard briefs that produce copies.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-12, MHJ-CX-30 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 14 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-112, MHJ-CL-049, MHJ-CL-105, MHJ-CL-044

### P25 Protect each specialist's strength; correct only what they missed

Keep collaborators' individuality, trim excess and pinch only the points they missed; vary direction by person; at scale, transmit context and intent and entrust the crew; accept a specialist's risky choice when it serves the whole.

- Limits: Coexists with deep hands-on checking of what she designed (MHJ-CL-152) — the tension is real and noted.
- Guards against: Every output converging on the director's style.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-30, MHJ-CX-13 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 13 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-113, MHJ-CL-114, MHJ-CL-115, MHJ-CL-116, MHJ-CL-043

### P26 Cast for sensibility and shared cause, not status

Choose collaborators for the specific sensibility the project needs and for aligned values, often newcomers or people from outside the genre, and build a crew that can later work with little explanation.

- Limits: Her stated casting criteria for performers (mood, values, budding potential) are on record, but who recruited and cast which NewJeans members is disputed (CX-22); do not credit her with all casting.
- Guards against: Hiring by reputation; mismatched teams.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-22 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 16 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-048, MHJ-CL-117, MHJ-CL-156

### P27 Produce the conditions, not the depiction

Qualities such as naturalness or improvisation in creative collaborators and performers cannot be staged; design the conditions that let them appear (trust, explained purpose, room to vary, kept accidents), and explain why each task matters.

- Limits: Evidence comes from performers and creative crews. Do not transfer it to service staff or users as a way to manufacture 'authentic' behaviour; that would be managed emotional labour (our caution).
- Guards against: Performed authenticity.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-28 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 14 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-025, MHJ-CL-119, MHJ-CL-154, MHJ-CL-051

### P28 Clear, sparing feedback *(supporting — stated stance, weaker evidence)*

Do not call weak work good; praise sparingly so 'good' carries information; state the right direction clearly and quickly.

- Limits: One event (School of Music 2024) carries most of the support; collaborators describe reassurance as much as sparing praise. Clarity is not harshness.
- Guards against: Feedback inflation; ambiguous direction.
- Evidence: directly stated, medium confidence, 4 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-106, MHJ-CL-149

## Stage VIII — Business & organisation

*What structure, budget and proof make it possible and durable?*

### P29 Constraint is the engine; think instead of spend

Treat budget and deadline as the frame that produces commercial creative work and ask what they make possible before asking for more; spend thinking before money.

- Limits: A stated preference, not evidence that less budget gives better results; no low-budget failures are recorded (survivorship). Never use it to underfund accessibility, testing, safety or staffing. In public services, finance, health, law or safety contexts, accuracy, accessibility and official wording come first; apply only where it cannot mislead or exclude anyone (our application).
- Guards against: Spending as a substitute for an idea.
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 10 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-131, MHJ-CL-132, MHJ-CL-110, MHJ-CL-150

### P30 Art and capital together (her stated stance)

Her stated stance: work that cannot sustain itself loses attention and vitality, so make the business carry the work; start from what you would want as a customer, refuse to sell what you would not, and win partners with the project's excitement rather than a revenue pitch.

- Limits: 'Money follows good work' is her belief, not a documented causal result; whether NewJeans' results owed more to planning or to capital is open (CX-23).
- Guards against: Art without a business model; business that hollows out the work.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-23, MHJ-CX-26 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 13 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-134, MHJ-CL-135, MHJ-CL-085, MHJ-CL-124

### P31 Fit the structure to the people; seek authority where outcomes are capped

Where a downstream result is capped by upstream decisions, seek influence over the upstream part — but combining creative and management roles is not universally better; fit the structure to how each person's potential is released.

- Limits: Never export 'one person must control everything' as a rule; her own caveat (MHJ-CL-125) is binding. In public services, finance, health, law or safety contexts, accuracy, accessibility and official wording come first; apply only where it cannot mislead or exclude anyone (our application).
- Guards against: Silo handoffs that kill the idea; also founder-control dogma.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-25, MHJ-CX-39 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 14 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-125, MHJ-CL-158, MHJ-CL-126, MHJ-CL-124

### P32 Prove with results; pair boldness with insurance

When argument cannot move an organisation, prove the point with a small result and let precedent become the system; pair every bold move with persuasion of the people who must do it and a prepared fallback.

- Limits: Small proofs must not harm anyone (her 'second-best route'). Proof-by-result is for creative and organisational questions, not for experiments on people's safety or rights.
- Guards against: Endless debate; reckless bets.
- Evidence: directly stated, high confidence, 10 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-120, MHJ-CL-148, MHJ-CL-122

### P33 Differentiated portfolio over clones of a winner *(supporting — stated stance, weaker evidence)*

A market stays alive through differentiated offers rather than copies of the latest success; diversity needs makers willing to try and audiences able to accept change.

- Limits: A stance about markets. Her organisational version (labels judged by results) was voiced mainly in the 2024 governance dispute and is not part of the rule.
- Guards against: Copy-the-hit strategy.
- Known tensions: MHJ-CX-44, MHJ-CX-40 — the rule is a default, not an absolute
- Evidence: directly stated, medium confidence, 5 independent sources; claims MHJ-CL-145
